Main.sentence: Valerie June Jarrett ( née Bowman ; born November 14, 1956)  is an American businesswoman and former government official, who has been the chief executive officer of the ___E:Obama Foundation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Obama_Foundation)___ since 2021.  She was the longest-serving ___E:senior advisor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senior_Advisor_to_the_President_of_the_United_States)___ to ___E:U.S. President U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States)___ ___E:Barack Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ .

She was assistant to the president for ___E:Public Engagement and Intergovernmental Affairs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_House_Office_of_Public_Engagement_and_Intergovernmental_Affairs)___ , overseeing the office of the same name, and chaired the ___E:White House Council on Women and Girls U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_House_Council_on_Women_and_Girls)___ .

Before that, she was the ___E:chief executive officer U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_executive_officer)___ of The Habitat Company and a co-chair of the ___E:Obama–Biden Transition Project U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Obama%E2%80%93Biden_Transition_Project)___ .

Jarrett was born in ___E:Shiraz U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shiraz)___ , Iran, during ___E:the Shah's U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mohammad_Reza_Pahlavi)___ rule, to American parents ___E:James E. Bowman U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_E._Bowman)___ and ___E:Barbara T. Bowman U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbara_T._Bowman)___ .

Her father, a pathologist and geneticist, worked at a hospital in Shiraz in 1956. When she was five years old, the family moved to ___E:London U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London)___ for a year, later moving to ___E:Chicago U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago)___ in 1962.

Her maternal great-grandfather, ___E:Robert Robinson Taylor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Robinson_Taylor)___ , was the first accredited African-American architect, and the first African-American student to enroll at the ___E:Massachusetts Institute of Technology U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massachusetts_Institute_of_Technology)___ .
Her maternal grandfather, ___E:Robert Rochon Taylor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Rochon_Taylor)___ , was chairman of the Chicago Housing Authority in the 1940s.
As a child, Jarrett spoke ___E:Persian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Persian_language)___ , ___E:French U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_language)___ , and English.

Her mother was one of four children's advocates who created the ___E:Erikson Institute U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erikson_Institute)___ in 1966. The institute was established to expand collective knowledge of ___E:child development U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Child_development)___ for teachers and other professionals working with young children.

Jarrett graduated from ___E:Northfield Mount Hermon School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northfield_Mount_Hermon_School)___ in 1974, and earned a B.A. in psychology from ___E:Stanford University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanford_University)___ in 1978 and a ___E:Juris Doctor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juris_Doctor)___ (J.D.) from the ___E:University of Michigan Law School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Michigan_Law_School)___ in 1981.

Jarrett got her start in ___E:Chicago U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago)___ politics in 1987 working for ___E:Mayor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayor_of_Chicago)___ ___E:Harold Washington U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harold_Washington)___  as deputy corporation counsel for finance and development.
Jarrett continued to work in the ___E:Chicago U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago)___ mayor's office in the 1990s.

She was deputy chief of staff for Mayor ___E:Richard Daley U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_M._Daley)___ , during which time (1991) she hired ___E:Michelle Robinson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michelle_Obama)___ (who was then engaged to ___E:Barack Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ ) from ___E:Sidley Austin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sidley_Austin)___ .

Jarrett served as commissioner of the department of planning and development from 1991 through 1995,  and she was chairwoman of the ___E:Chicago Transit Authority U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Transit_Authority)___ from 1995 to 2003.
From 1995 to 2009, Jarrett was the CEO of The Habitat Company, a real estate development and management company.
She was replaced as CEO by Mark Sega when she joined the Obama administration.

Daniel E. Levin was the chairman of Habitat, which was formed in 1971.  Jarrett was a member of the board of ___E:Chicago Stock Exchange U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Stock_Exchange)___ (2000–2007, as chairman, 2004–2007).

Jarrett was a member of the ___E:board of trustees U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Board_of_trustees)___ of the ___E:University of Chicago Medical Center U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Chicago_Medical_Center)___ from 1996 to 2009, becoming vice chairwoman in 2002 and chairwoman in 2006.  She also served as chairwoman of the ___E:Chicago Transit Board U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Transit_Board)___  and vice chairwoman of the board of trustees of the ___E:University of Chicago U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Chicago)___ .

She was a trustee of the ___E:Museum of Science and Industry U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Museum_of_Science_and_Industry_(Chicago))___ in Chicago  and a board member of the ___E:Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Reserve_Bank_of_Chicago)___ .
Jarrett serves on the board of directors of ___E:USG Corporation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USG_Corporation)___ , a Chicago-based building materials corporation.

Jarrett was President Obama's longest serving advisor, confidante and was "widely tipped for a high-profile position in an Obama administration." The Wall Street Journal's Douglas Belkin was quoted saying

Unlike ___E:Bert Lance U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bert_Lance)___ , who arrived from ___E:Georgia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgia_(U.S._state))___ with President ___E:[Jimmy] Carter U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Carter)___ and became his budget director, or ___E:Karen Hughes U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karen_Hughes)___ , who was President ___E:[George W.] Bush U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush)___ 's communications manager, Ms. Jarrett isn't a confidante with a particular portfolio.
What she does share with these counterparts is a fierce sense of loyalty and a refusal to publicly say anything that may reflect poorly on the candidate—or steal his thunder.

On November 14, 2008, President-elect Barack Obama selected Jarrett to serve as a ___E:senior advisor to the president U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senior_Advisor_to_the_President_of_the_United_States)___ and ___E:assistant to the president for intergovernmental relations and public liaison U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_House_Office_of_Public_Engagement_and_Intergovernmental_Affairs)___ .
Jarrett was one of three senior advisors to President Obama.

She held the retitled position of assistant to the president for intergovernmental affairs and public engagement,  managed the ___E:White House Office of Public Engagement and Intergovernmental Affairs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_House_Office_of_Public_Engagement_and_Intergovernmental_Affairs)___ , and ___E:Office of Urban Affairs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Office_of_Urban_Affairs)___ ; she also chaired the ___E:White House Council on Women and Girls U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_House_Council_on_Women_and_Girls)___ and the White House Office of Olympic, Paralympic, and Youth Sport.
She was part of the ___E:U.S. State Visit to the UK U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._State_Visit_to_the_UK)___ in May 2011.
She said that the 2011 report Women in America , which the administration produced for the Council on Women and Girls, would be used to guide policy-making.
Jarrett had a staff of approximately three dozen and received full-time ___E:Secret Service U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secret_Service)___ protection.

Jarrett's role as both a friend of the Obamas and as senior advisor in the White House was controversial: in his memoirs ___E:Robert M. Gates U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_M._Gates)___ , former ___E:secretary of defense U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Defense)___ , discussed his objection to her involvement in foreign security affairs;  ___E:David Axelrod U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Axelrod_(political_consultant))___ reported in his memoirs about ___E:Rahm Emanuel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rahm_Emanuel)___ 's attempts to have her selected as Obama's replacement in the senate, due to concerns about the difficulty in working with a family friend in a major policy role.
In addition to being senior advisor to the president, Jarrett held other leadership positions and completed further duties.

Among those included chairing the ___E:White House Council on Women and Girls U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_House_Council_on_Women_and_Girls)___ and co-chairing the ___E:White House Task Force to Protect Students from Sexual Assault U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_House_Task_Force_to_Protect_Students_from_Sexual_Assault)___ .

In March 2014, she participated as a speaker on ___E:Voices in Leadership U:(https://www.hsph.harvard.edu/voices/)___ , an original ___E:Harvard T. H. Chan School of Public Health U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvard_T.H._Chan_School_of_Public_Health)___ webcast series, in a discussion entitled, " ___E:Leadership in the White House U:(https://www.hsph.harvard.edu/voices/events/jarrett/)___ ," moderated by ___E:Dr. Atul Gawande U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atul_Gawande)___ .
In 1991, as deputy chief of staff to Mayor Richard Daley, Jarrett interviewed Michelle Robinson, the then-fiancé to future President Barack Obama, for an opening in the mayor's office.
She immediately offered Robinson the job afterwards.
Robinson asked for time to think and also asked Jarrett to meet Obama.
Robinson accepted the job with the mayor's office after meeting for dinner.

It was at this time that Jarrett reportedly took the couple under her wing and "introduced them to a wealthier and better-connected Chicago than their own."  When Jarrett later left her position at the mayor's office to head the Chicago department of planning and development, Michelle Obama went with her.

Obama's election team and supporters, for example at the Philadelphia National Constitution Center speech, included Valerie Jarrett, David Plouffe and David Axelrod, all whom later joined him and First Lady Michelle Obama in the White House.
Since leaving the White House, Jarrett has volunteered as a senior advisor to the ___E:Obama Foundation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Obama_Foundation)___ .

She joined the ___E:board of directors U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Board_of_directors)___ of ___E:Ariel Investments U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ariel_Investments)___ ,  ___E:2U, Inc. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2U_(company))___ ,  ___E:Lyft U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyft)___ ,  ___E:Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kennedy_Center_for_the_Performing_Arts)___ ,  ___E:Walgreens Boots Alliance U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walgreens_Boots_Alliance)___ , ___E:Ralph Lauren Corporation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ralph_Lauren_Corporation)___ , ___E:Sweetgreen U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sweetgreen)___ ,  and is a member of the ___E:Goldman Sachs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goldman_Sachs)___ One Million Black Women advisory council.
She served as the co-chair of the United State of Women,  chair of the Board of When We All Vote and Civic Nation,   and a senior advisor to ___E:ATTN: U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ATTN:)___ .
In January 2018 she became a distinguished senior fellow at the ___E:University of Chicago Law School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Chicago_Law_School)___ .
In July 2017 Jarrett signed a deal with ___E:Viking Press U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viking_Press)___ for her book titled Finding My Voice: My Journey to the West Wing and the Path Forward .
It was published in 2019.

In December 2020, following the announcement that Obama Foundation President ___E:Wally Adeyemo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wally_Adeyemo)___ would be nominated to become ___E:Deputy Secretary of the Treasury U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Deputy_Secretary_of_the_Treasury)___ , the Foundation announced that Jarrett would take over his duties on an interim basis until a successor can be found.
Jarrett has served as ___E:chief executive officer U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_executive_officer)___ of the Foundation since 2021 and is a member of the board of directors.

Along with ___E:Donna Brazile U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donna_Brazile)___ , vice chairwoman of the ___E:Democratic National Committee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_National_Committee)___ , she is one of the political figures to make a ___E:cameo appearance U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameo_appearance)___ as herself in the ___E:CBS U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS)___ drama The Good Wife .
In 1983 she married William Robert Jarrett, son of Chicago Sun-Times reporter ___E:Vernon Jarrett U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vernon_Jarrett)___ .
She attributes her switch from a private to a public career to the birth of their daughter, and her own desire to do something that would make their daughter proud.

Her daughter, ___E:Laura Jarrett U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Jarrett)___ , would go on to become an attorney and reporter for ___E:CNN U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CNN)___ , and is now a senior legal correspondent for ___E:NBC News U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC_News)___ and co-anchor of the ___E:Saturday edition U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weekend_Today)___ of Today ,    and daughter-in-law of the Canadian politician ___E:Bas Balkissoon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bas_Balkissoon)___ .
She separated from her husband in 1987 and they were divorced in 1988.

In 2018, a ___E:tweet U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twitter#Tweets)___ by ___E:Roseanne Barr U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roseanne_Barr)___ disparaged her. Barr said, in reference to Jarrett, it was as though the " ___E:Muslim Brotherhood U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muslim_Brotherhood)___ and ___E:Planet of the Apes U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Planet_of_the_Apes)___ had a baby".
Subsequently, Barr was sanctioned by her talent agency ___E:ICM Partners U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ICM_Partners)___ , losing the lead role on her eponymous television program, Roseanne .
